historical_reviews.v3_1: The Table 35-12 all-events control is dangerously broad, so normal coverage must use an explicit selected-event mask unless the owner separately approves all-event re-arm.

original_test_intent: Re-arm one approved latched assertion or deassertion event for one verified sensor, force a bounded status refresh, and prove the outcome without erasing the original fault history or masking a still-active condition.
original_method: Master remains TBD. Review identifies IPMI v2.0 Table 35-12 raw 0x04/0x2A with sensor number, explicit all-versus-selected control and event-type-correct assertion/deassertion mask bytes.
manual_activity: The monitoring owner approves the dedicated target, sensor, exact selected assertion/deassertion bit, current fault disposition, expected latch transition, maintenance window and escalation if the condition remains active.
required_inputs: Sensor re-arm support and manual/auto re-arm semantics
Current raw 0x04/0x2B event-status and 0x29 enable baseline
Independent proof that the originating fault is cleared or intentionally active
safety_requirements: Do not use broad all-event re-arm by default
Do not re-arm a live safety fault merely to silence its latch
Validate reserved bits and event-type mapping
Stop on event storm, unavailable status or ambiguous refresh
agent_execution_scope: Verify sensor identity, SDR event type and re-arm capability
Capture event status, enable state, current reading and preserved logs
Confirm fault disposition and exact selected bit
Present the complete variable-length 0x2A payload for approval
Poll boundedly through reading/state-unavailable and read 0x2B/0x29
Correlate any regenerated event with the still-active condition
Archive the original and post-rearm timelines
engineer_actions: Approve the selected event and live-fault handling
Own physical fault recovery or escalation

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek correctly refuses the TBD action; the standard command is usable only with target-specific event identity, status semantics and explicit owner approval.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, issue one secret-safe raw 0x04 0x2a <sensor> <all-or-selected-control> [assertion-mask-LS assertion-mask-MS deassertion-mask-LS deassertion-mask-MS] request using the Table 35-12 form for the sensor's threshold or discrete event type; verify with raw 0x04 0x2b <sensor> and 0x04 0x29 <sensor>.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: No Master sensor, mask or oracle is invented; source TBD and 10/5 timing remain preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use one selected-event re-arm after preserving history and proving the fault context, then wait only through a bounded sensor-update interval and distinguish latch clearing, event regeneration and persistent physical fault.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a narrowly scoped, evidence-preserving Review procedure without changing the Master TBD.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: This does not clear SEL, repair the cause, change event enables or prove all sensor events can be re-armed.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A re-arm may immediately regenerate an event when the condition remains active; repeated re-arm can obscure chronology and create noise.

project_override_considerations: A vendor API is equivalent only if it targets the same sensor and exact event latch, exposes update-in-progress/status evidence and does not clear event history.
expected_evidence: Pre-action reading, 0x2B status, 0x29 enable state and preserved logs
Exact 0x2A control and assertion/deassertion mask bytes
Post-action status plus any regenerated event correlation
Proof that SEL/history, enables, thresholds and unrelated sensors were unchanged

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title consistently identifies Re-arm Sensor Events while Procedure and Criteria are TBD. Missing target event, payload, live-fault rules and acceptance semantics plus generic log clearing are omissions, not contradictory source requirements; the Review mapping is conditional and preserves Master TBD.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The standard operation is identifiable. Sensor/event identity, fault state, selected mask and expected status are Project readiness inputs; execution becomes BLOCKED if a live condition cannot be distinguished safely.

review_improvement: Constrains re-arm to one selected latch, preserves pre-existing evidence and explicitly distinguishes a cleared latch from immediate regeneration caused by a persistent fault.
independent_technical_reasoning: Re-arm requests a sensor to refresh event status and may regenerate messages for conditions still present. It is not equivalent to clearing the fault or its historical record. Because the all-events form can affect every latch on the sensor, the safe default is a single capability-checked assertion/deassertion bit with pre/post 0x2B evidence and no repeated suppression.
